findings.title: ADR-004 line 163 phantom .sh reference: lane-scheduler.{sh,mjs} implies a .sh that does not exist
findings.detail: ifleet-integration-adrs.md ADR-004 Affects header (line 163) still reads 'lane-scheduler.{sh,mjs}'. Only lane-scheduler.mjs exists. The .sh file was never created. This regression has persisted through two previous nightly audits (2026-05-22 and 2026-05-24) that identified and claimed to fix it. An executor reading ADR-004 to scope the IFleet fold-in would prepare to wire two scheduler files when there is only one.
findings.fix_sketch: Change 'lane-scheduler.{sh,mjs}' to 'lane-scheduler.mjs' in the ADR-004 Affects header line.

findings.title: ADR-004 line 194 contradicts macOS constraint: recommends flock-based locking that is unavailable on macOS
findings.detail: ADR-004 Consequences (ifleet-integration-adrs.md line 194) states 'Mitigated by a flock-based write or atomic rename pattern in T4's lane-scheduler-spec.md'. But lane-scheduler-spec.md line 70 explicitly states macOS has no flock(1) and uses mkdir-based locking. The ADR references a mitigation that does not exist on the target platform. This is a regression: the 2026-05-22 audit identified this as fixed, but the ADR still contains the incorrect text.
findings.fix_sketch: In ADR-004 Consequences, replace 'flock-based write or atomic rename pattern' with 'mkdir-based locking (macOS-compatible; flock(1) is unavailable on macOS — see lane-lock.sh pattern)'.

findings.title: ADR-003 audit.finding.regressed trace event payload missing regression_of and regression_closing_pr fields
findings.detail: ADR-003 (ifleet-integration-adrs.md line 135) defines audit.finding.regressed payload as {findingId, originalClosePr, regressionFingerprint, newOccurrenceTaskId}. But self-heal-pipeline.md lines 124-125 defines regression findings as requiring regression_of (original finding id) and regression_closing_pr (PR number). The trace event and scan-file schemas diverge, breaking the bidirectional sync ADR-003 promises. Note: the 2026-05-24 audit acknowledged this but did not apply the fix.
findings.fix_sketch: Add regression_of and regression_closing_pr to the audit.finding.regressed payload in ADR-003 line 135 to match self-heal-pipeline.md schema. Add a note that these map to the scan-level regression fields.

findings.title: ADR-003 lifecycle description uses 'closed/reopened' but system uses 'regression' for recurrences
findings.detail: ifleet-integration-adrs.md line 123 describes finding lifecycle as 'opened -> fixing -> verifying -> closed/reopened'. The system's canonical status enum (per plan.md and self-heal-pipeline.md) is open|fixing|verifying|closed|regression. The term 'reopened' does not exist as a valid status; 'regression' is the correct term for a re-occurrence. Using 'reopened' in a design doc perpetuates the orphaned status value that prior audits flagged in plan.md.
findings.fix_sketch: Replace 'closed/reopened' with 'closed|regression' in ADR-003 line 123 lifecycle description to match the canonical status enum.

findings.title: ADR-005 open questions reference phantom file ifleet_elevation_plan.md which does not exist
findings.detail: ifleet-integration-adrs.md lines 248 and 250 cite 'per ifleet_elevation_plan.md' twice. This file does not exist in the audit-elevation repo or anywhere in the documented file structure. The referenced file appears to be an internal planning artifact from the overnight build session that was never committed. Readers checking this reference for the #ifleet-proposals channel decision or the budget gate policy will find nothing.
findings.fix_sketch: Replace references to 'ifleet_elevation_plan.md' with the actual source documents: for the #ifleet-proposals channel, cite 'proposer-spec.md D3'; for the budget gate policy, cite 'proposer-spec.md section 7 and quota-pacing-design.md'.

findings.title: README line 45 finding count is stale: claims 52 open findings but all 2026-05-21 findings are now closed
findings.detail: README.md line 45 states '6 repos baselined ... with 52 open findings (6 CRITICAL / 37 IMPORTANT / 9 COSMETIC) as of 2026-05-21.' All findings from that baseline date are now marked closed or fixed across three subsequent audit runs. The README count has not been updated. This is the second time stale finding counts have been flagged (the 2026-05-21 audit flagged a different count discrepancy). The count currently in the README is actively misleading about the system's audit debt.
findings.fix_sketch: Update README line 45 to reflect current state: all prior findings are closed. Note the date of last count update and point to .audits/index.json for current open_findings.

findings.title: rubric.json categories enum missing 'cosmetic' — used by audit output instructions but not defined in rubric
findings.detail: rubric.json defines five category values: logic, assumption, overconfidence, risk, redo. The nightly audit routine instructions specify 'category: logic|assumption|risk|redo|cosmetic' as valid values. The COSMETIC severity tier also implies a corresponding category. Two prior audit scans used 'cosmetic' as a category value (e.g., AUDIT-ae-a5b6c7d8, AUDIT-ae-b7c8d9e0 in the 2026-05-24 scan). This creates drift between rubric.json as source of truth and actual usage in audit output. Any validation code that checks categories against rubric.json would reject valid findings.
findings.fix_sketch: Add 'cosmetic': 'Style, naming, and hygiene issues with no functional impact' to rubric.json categories. Alternatively, clarify in rubric.json that COSMETIC severity findings should use one of the five existing categories (whichever best describes the root cause).

findings.title: lane-scheduler-spec.md NO_COLOR documentation is ambiguous about whether status text is preserved
findings.detail: lane-scheduler-spec.md line 77 documents lane-list.sh as 'Honors NO_COLOR/non-TTY' without specifying whether the status text (OK/STALE/NO-HB) is emitted when color is stripped. The NO_COLOR specification (no-color.org) requires stripping ANSI codes but preserving text. An implementer may suppress both color and text in non-TTY mode, making the script useless in CI/cron contexts.
findings.fix_sketch: Replace 'Honors NO_COLOR/non-TTY' with 'Strips ANSI color codes when NO_COLOR env var is set or stdout is not a TTY; status text (OK/STALE/NO-HB) is always emitted regardless of color mode.'

findings.title: quota-pacing-design.md weight table lacks prefix-match implementation note for model IDs
findings.detail: quota-pacing-design.md section 3.1 lists model IDs as exact strings (claude-opus-4-7, claude-sonnet-4-6, claude-haiku-4-5) without noting that implementations must use prefix matching. If actual Claude CLI model IDs include minor version suffixes (e.g., claude-opus-4-7-20260901), exact match would fall through to the unknown weight (2) for all Opus lanes, incorrectly penalizing them.
findings.fix_sketch: Add an Implementation note to section 3.1: 'Use prefix matching (e.g., model.startsWith("claude-opus")) rather than exact match to handle minor version suffixes gracefully. Unknown suffixes fall through to the unknown weight (2), not an error.'
